rationale.region: Regions are coarse on purpose so an event and an outlet can match without exact city agreement. Wezoree runs a Detroit wedding and Loverly runs Michigan albums, so michigan stays its own value; tag a Michigan event with both michigan and midwest_us. The European and Latin values come from what Wezoree, Wed Vibes, The Lane and Brides actually publish: Italy, France, Spain, Portugal and Greece fold into mediterranean_europe, Scotland, Ireland and England into british_isles, Mexico and Puerto Rico into mexico_caribbean. international_other catches Africa, Asia and the rest (Wezoree ran Kenya and Romania).
rationale.landscape_venue: Mostly lifted from Loverly's published setting filters (garden, vineyard, beach, mountain, woods, lake, ranch, barn, desert, museum, art gallery, restaurant, country club, hotel, loft) and Carats & Cake's venue directory (resort and hotel, estates, vineyards, gardens, beach and waterfront). Barn, ranch and field are merged into farm_ranch_countryside. backyard_private_home covers The Anti-Bride and Brides backyard and family-home weddings. museum_gallery reflects Brides features at the Met, Field Museum and Baltimore Museum of Art. island_tropical is the obvious gap for destination coverage at Wezoree and Wed Vibes.
rationale.architecture: Built-form values named in recent features: Ashford Castle and a French chateau (Wezoree), Villa Palmieri and Villa Bettoni (The Lane, Wezoree), Hedsor House and Commodore Perry Estate (historic manor), Hamilton Loft and Race and Religious (industrial loft), Cambridge Mill in Detroit (brick_historic_urban). Kept separate from landscape_venue so a barn venue can match on setting without claiming rustic timber architecture. adobe_hacienda, mid_century_modern, art_deco, church_cathedral and ballroom_grand_hall are gap-fillers for Southwest, Palm Springs, and Michigan venues that outlets feature but do not list as filters.
rationale.aesthetic: The first seven are Loverly's published style filters (classic, romantic, whimsical, modern, boho, glamorous, alternative). fashion_forward_editorial covers The Anti-Bride, The Lane, Vogue and Over The Moon, which all lead with fashion. bold_color_maximalist and organic_textural split color-led work from texture-led work (The Anti-Bride bold prints, Wed Vibes mirrored disco balls, Brides vibrant palettes). culturally_rooted reflects Carats & Cake, Brides, Vogue and Wezoree explicitly seeking cultural range. intimate_micro covers elopements and micro-weddings (The Anti-Bride, Brides). playful_party covers Over The Moon fun and Brides party-first weddings. moody_dramatic and vintage_heritage fill gaps seen in Loverly and Brides headlines.
rationale.dress_style: Outlets rarely publish a dress filter, so this is derived from what their copy highlights: Vogue wedding suits, a stylist bride with several looks, vintage Dior and Danielle Frankel; Brides three Oscar de la Renta gowns; The Anti-Bride couples in bold colours or prints; Over The Moon shop categories (bridal, getting ready, guest dressing, black tie, resort formal); Loverly's suits and tuxedos shop. Silhouette values (ball_gown, a_line_classic, sheath_column, slip_minimalist, lace_romantic) are the obvious gap so event data can be tagged by gown even when the outlet does not.
rationale.season: Outlets frame weddings seasonally (Brides spring weddings, Vogue fall and winter guest edits, Loverly winter content, Over The Moon holiday and fall edits). The four-season split is too coarse for Michigan, where early fall color and late fall are different markets, so summer and fall are subdivided, and holiday_season is called out because Over The Moon and Vogue both run holiday edits. year_round_climate is for tropical and desert destinations where season carries no editorial meaning.
